newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduras authorizes corn, bean exports.
newsitem.headline: Honduras authorizes corn, bean exports.

text.p: Honduras has lifted a temporary ban on the export of corn and beans, authorities said over the weekend.
The government of this poor Central America country had placed a ban on exporting the two food staples a month ago in order to create a "strategic reserve."
"The exporting of corn and beans has been authorized once again considering that now we have created the strategic reserve," Julio Gonzalez, the deputy economy minister, told reporters.

The government used the time to acquire 55,000 quintales (100-pound or 46-kg bags) of beans and 25,000 quintales of corn to cover seasonal shortages, Deputy Agriculture Minister Marco Micheletti said. That stockpile may be increased through imports, he said.
Demand is greater than the supply of corn and beans in Honduras, largely because of exports to neighboring El Salvador, Guatemala and Nicaragua.
"There should be free enterprise but not at the expense of the Honduran people," Micheletti said.
